I need to understand the full picture of seat counting.

The invitation service currently counts all active members and pending invitations, then requests one seat per invite. It should instead count only billable roles. I am deciding whether to filter existing counts or add new ones.

`countActiveMembers` is also used for `memberCount` in organization-service, which is a display count of all members rather than a seat limit. Changing it would break tests that expect 4 members including viewers. Tests in tenant-scope and jobs.test.ts expect 4 seats used after seeding 4 members.

Tests expect free-plan members to be rejected when the seat limit is 3, even if the viewer is included.

Billable members are now 3, so the org is at quota and should reject new member invites. Viewer invites should still succeed. The plan-limits test counts all active members, not just billable seats, so it will need updating if that count function changes.

The tenant-scope test claims to count seats per organization, but it actually expects 4 active members.

Excluding viewers from `countActiveMembers` would make the seat test expect 3 instead of 4. The function name implies active members, not seats. I need to check how `memberCount` is asserted and review Drizzle role queries. The plan is to add `isBillableRole` in member.ts and update seat counting logic.

Seat counting should be filtered to billable roles in usage recompute, pending invitations, seatsUsed, and requested seats. `countActiveMembers` may remain unchanged since the invitation service uses it for seat enforcement.

The tenant-scope test expects 4 active members, not seats. Since `countActiveMembers` counts all members, the assertion remains valid and needs no update. Billable role filtering will be applied only inside the invitation service.

Changing `countActiveMembers` to billable-only would break the plan-limits test. The invitation service currently adds all active members and pending invitations. I will add optional role filters or new functions instead of altering existing count functions.

The member.removed event is missing its role field.

The usage service needs the member's role to decrement correctly after removal. The event payload only includes memberId and userId. I could look up the archived member's role before decrementing, or add the role field to the event. Tests use toMatchObject so extra fields are safe.

I'll look up the archived member's role in the listener rather than changing the event contract. The role_changed delta is +1 when a viewer becomes billable, -1 when a billable becomes a viewer, and 0 otherwise. I need to subscribe to member.role_changed in registerUsageListeners.

The invite form disables invites when seats are exhausted regardless of role.

Viewer invites must bypass seat quota checks in both the UI form and the invite-member action. The form currently blocks all submissions when seats are full, which would wrongly refuse viewer-only batches. The action also unconditionally rejects any new invite based on total usage, so it needs to skip the limit check for viewers.

The accept-invitation action checks seats after the member joins. Since the stored usage counter only tracks active members, a viewer joining does not increase it and passes the check. The seat increment happens via event listener before the check runs.

The updateMemberRoleAction must check seat availability before writing any changes. If the service throws an error, the action's assertLastOwnerRetained guard prevents the role from being updated.

The seat quota for role changes counts billable active members plus pending billable invitations. A viewer being upgraded is not yet in the active count, so adding one is correct. The spec treats suspended viewers as non-active, which means they do not count toward the limit.

The spec requires counting a seat for any viewer-to-billable role change, even if the member is suspended. This creates a mismatch with the stored usage counter, which only tracks active members.

The seat quota check uses an invitation-style live count of active billable members plus pending billable invites. The stored usage counter only tracks active members and excludes pending invites.

Incremental adjustments to the counter are +1 for billable joins, -1 for billable removals, and boundary checks during role changes.

The updateMemberRole action does not verify member status, so it could process role changes on archived members.

The role-change event payload lacks member status. I will look up the member after the update to verify they are active before adjusting the seat counter. If the member is not active, no seat delta should apply.

The seat quota check will refuse any viewer-to-billable role change if the live count would exceed the limit, regardless of whether the member is active. The stored usage counter only increments for active members, so a suspended member promoted while at quota will not increase it. The event listener must verify member status before updating the counter.

The role-change listener will fetch the member by ID and skip the seat counter update if the member is inactive or archived. It calculates a delta from the old and new roles and increments usage only when the delta is non-zero. The removed listener must also decrement usage for archived members who were billable.

The removed listener must avoid double-decrementing for suspended members. The old code decremented usage unconditionally on member removal, but the new counter only tracks active members. A suspended billable member was never counted, so subtracting one would be incorrect.

The old incremental counter was naive. The user requires adjustments and a full recount to always agree. A removed member's role remains on the row, but archiving sets status to suspended, so the listener cannot tell whether the member was active before removal. The service should compute the seat delta before mutation instead of relying solely on listeners.

The recount logic should count only active, unarchived members with billable roles. To fix the drift, the remove event must include the member's previous status and role so the listener can subtract one seat only when the member was previously active and billable.

Adding the member's role to the removed event would fix the drift but may be overkill. A simpler approach is to compute the seat delta directly in the member service before archiving, then let the listener apply it from the event. This avoids duplicating logic between the service and the listener.

The member.removed event will include the member's role from before removal. The listener will only decrement the seat counter when that pre-removal status was active, preventing incorrect decrements for suspended members.

The removed event payload will include the member's role. Only one emitter site exists, so adding a required field is safe. The jobs test must be updated from 4 to 3 seatsUsed because it validates against the recount.

The invitation free plan test still rejects new invites after recount because the live count of 3 active members plus 1 pending invite exceeds the limit of 3. The bulk growth test also remains valid since 4 active members plus 49 invites still exceeds the 50 seat cap.

The invitation-service bulk test still passes. After the change, the org reaches 8 seats with 9 active members, so the batch of 2 members is correctly rejected. A single invite remains allowed because 9 does not exceed the 10-seat cap. The test comment is stale but the behavior is unchanged.

The invitation-service bulk test comment still claims 4 active members count as seats. I will update that comment and the arithmetic to reflect the new rule, since the user asked to correct visible tests.

The invitation-service bulk test comment still claims 4 active members count as seats. Updating it to 3 billable plus 5 fillers would make the remaining seat count 2, which would allow a batch of 2 members instead of rejecting it. The comment must be rewritten to reflect the new rule without changing the actual filler count, since the existing assertions still pass.

The invitation-service bulk test must be updated because the batch of 2 members would now succeed instead of failing. I will insert 6 fillers to reach 9 billable seats, or change the assertion. The plan-limits bulk test still correctly rejects new invites after recount.

The invite action pre-check must count only billable roles. It currently blocks viewer invites when the stored counter plus one exceeds the limit, even though the service allows them.
The UI blocks all invites once seats are exhausted.
The member service "Must call" list is missing `wouldExceedLimit`.

Subscription seats in seed data represent purchased counts, not usage.

Plan numbers remain unchanged. For member removals, the listener will load the member by ID to check their role before decrementing seats. Only billable roles will trigger a seat reduction; suspended members are excluded. The suspended-then-removed edge case is pre-existing drift.

The event payload will include the member's role. The listener will check this field to decide whether to decrement a seat. This prevents double-counting already-suspended billable members.

The event type will remain unchanged to minimize blast radius. Role change listeners will use from/to deltas, but only apply them when the member is active and not archived. New members will be counted as billable if their role is billable. The billable role list will be defined in member.ts.

The billable role list will be exported as `BILLABLE_ROLES` alongside the `isBillableRole` helper. Repositories can import this constant directly to avoid maintaining duplicate role definitions.

Invitation requests containing only non-billable roles must bypass the seat quota check entirely. Calling `wouldExceedLimit` with zero requested seats would incorrectly reject an already-full plan, since `used + 0 > limit` evaluates to true even when the organization is at capacity.

The invitation check will only run when requested seats are greater than zero. Role changes that promote a member to a billable role will verify the seat limit against active plus pending billable members before throwing an error. The existing invite message already references seats and can be reused. Seat quota validation must occur before any database write.

The seat check will run before `updateMemberRole`, after the last owner guard, so any throw leaves the database unchanged. To avoid heavy imports in `member-service`, a shared `seatsInUse` helper should live in a common module; placing it in `invitation-service` would risk circular dependencies.

A `seatsInUse` helper will be placed in a shared module or repository. It will sum billable active members and pending billable invitations. This avoids importing between member-service and invitation-service.

`countSeatsInUse` will live in `services/usage-service.ts`. It can safely import member and invitation repositories there. Both services will call this single function. The invite form must still allow viewer invites when the seat limit is exhausted.

The invite form will disable the email input and submit button only when the requested role is billable and seats are exhausted. The role selector must remain enabled so users can still switch to a viewer role. An alert may still appear to indicate the seat limit.

Accepting an invitation will skip the seat check for viewer roles. The invite action will only block billable roles when usage plus one exceeds the seat limit, though it relies on stored usage that excludes pending invites, so it may allow or block before the service validates the full count. Double-consumption of rate limits is pre-existing and out of scope. Tests will need updating.

Test expectations need updating to reflect the new seat accounting. `jobs.test.ts` should expect `seatsUsed` to be 3 instead of 4. `plan-limits.test.ts` must change its usage count from 4 to 3, and its test name should drop the old "reports the plan, the usage" wording that assumes all four members are billable. The invitation-service bulk seat math test needs an extra filler member so billable seats total 9, making `countActiveMembers` 10; its comment also needs updating. The `createTenant` fixture seeds four active members but only three are billable.

The invitation bulk seat test needs six filler members to reach nine billable seats and ten active members. Its comment must drop the old "4 from createTenant" wording. No new tests are needed for the viewer invite edge case.
The createTenant function does not set usage.

Capture seat occupancy before removal by checking active and billable status. Include role in the event for the listener to decide. Suspended members were already removed from the live set, so they do not affect billable counts.

The role field will be taken from the pre-archive snapshot. Removal events represent members who were live before archiving.

Snapshotting the member's active and billable status before archiving so the listener can safely decrement the seat count.

`isBillableRole` now explicitly checks for owner, admin, and member roles. Pending invitations are excluded from seat counts because they are not yet accepted or revoked. The existing `countPendingInvitations` function remains unchanged since it is used by tests to count all pending rows.
